text:
mike: Heads up — seeing persistent tail latency on dedicated-slice allocs in rack r12. graphs point to NIC tx-queue saturation on nodes hosting mix of dadi+shared tenants.
jess: ugh. is this the same bursty tenant we saw last week or a new noisy neighbor?
mike: different tenant id. pattern: small frequent bursts (~50–200 reqs/s) that keep NIC queue occupancy high and cause kernel packet drops. tcp_retransmits spike.
sara: any tcpdump or ethtool stats? can we confirm it's not a driver regression?
mike: quick capture attached to S3 (s3://redwood-debug/r12-nic-sat-17645.pcap). ethtool shows tx-queue full, irq coalescing looks normal. snippet: `Tx queue length: 512
packets sent: 1.2M
packet drops: 6.3k`
kyle: ops-bot posted an alert earlier: "egress-queue: r12 nodes crossing 85% tx occupancy". Ops-bot: :rotating_light: triggered 2:10 UTC.
jess: is this limited to r12 AZ or cross-rack?
mike: mostly r12, but a few spillovers to adjacent racks when we failover. suspect warm-pool backfill putting dedi slices on noisy hosts.
sara: could we backfill from a quieter pool instead of nearest warm slot? Tradeoff: a bit higher cross-az latency vs avoiding tail spikes.
jess: we need a short-term mitigation + long-term plan. short-term: throttle noisy tenant at proxy? set limiter at proxy for that tenant to cap egress TPS.
kyle: agreed. proxy limiter is fastest. downside: customer-visible throttling, cost to customer and potential SLO blips.
mike: also possible to prefer anti-affinity when placing dedi slices — keep dedicated tenants off hosts with high shared-tenant churn.
sara: long-term: consider fractional dedicated slices (smaller granularity) so noisy tenant consumes less contiguous tx bandwidth from a host. But that adds scheduler complexity.
jess: fractional slices = more packing, maybe worse for noisy cases if you pack more tenants per GPU. need simulation.
ops-bot: runbook note: if queue drops > 5k in 15m -> escalate to network oncall.
kyle: cost discussion: if we steer away from warmers and prefer cold fills to avoid noisy hosts, that increases cold-starts and GPU spinup/idle costs. Estimate +12% infra cost for r12 to keep tail < 95th.
mike: can we instead do egress shaping on host level: per-tenant egress policer in host kernel netfilter? less customer-visible than proxy throttle, transparent shaping.
sara: kernel policer could be effective but we need perf testing — netfilter rules can add CPU overhead on hot hosts.
jess: action items: 1) kyle -> deploy proxy limiter for tenant T-847 (in 10m, rollback on SLO hits). 2) mike -> attach more pcap+ethtool logs and run NIC firmware health check. 3) sara -> run cost simulation for warm-vs-cold fill and fractional-slice tradeoffs. 4) devex-bot -> post a short status to #customer-success if proxy limiter goes live.
kyle: starting limiter rollout now, 10% at t0, 100% in 5m if no regressions.
mike: I'll run nic firmware check and report in 15m.
sara: also propose we add a new metric to console: per-dedicated-slice tx-queue-occupancy so product can set per-tenant isolation thresholds.
jess: good. capture that as a feature request in the roadmap doc and flag for infra/product sync next week.
devex-bot: friendly note -> please avoid posting full pcaps in public channels. use s3 ACL=internal.
mike: noted. pcap already uploaded with internal ACL.
kyle: limiter at 100% now. monitoring 5m window. so far p95 latency trending down in r12.
jess: thumbs up. we'll keep this thread as the short-term incident log and iterate on longer-term scheduler/packaging proposals.
